title: Register StartingPositionCalendarMode with the shared expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices harness instead of the ad hoc single-viewport check

evidence.quote:
// To add a new dialog/screen to the guard, add a `testWidgets` case in
// `test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart` that calls this helper

why: The repo already built and documented expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices specifically for this class of regression (RenderFlex overflow at extreme device/text-scale corners), with an explicit extension point at test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart. StartingPositionCalendarMode — the exact widget that shipped a 'BOTTOM OVERFLOWED BY 59 PIXELS' bug — was never added there (grepped test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart for 'StartingPositionCalendarMode'/'Starting': no match). Instead this batch's test hand-rolls a single fixed corner (375×500 @ 2.0x text scale) and asserts on implementation details (a SingleChildScrollView exists; no Spacer exists) rather than the systematic multi-corner check the rest of the codebase relies on. A future edit that reintroduces overflow at a different corner (e.g. the narrow 280×653 or 1.3x scale the shared matrix covers) would ship undetected by this file, and the general-purpose guard would never learn about this widget either.
recommendation: Add a testWidgets case for StartingPositionCalendarMode to test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart using expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices with the required provider overrides; keep or retire the structural (SingleChildScrollView/Spacer) assertions as a secondary, narrower regression check if desired.
acceptance_criteria: test/overflow/overflow_guard_test.dart includes a case pumping StartingPositionCalendarMode through expectNoOverflowAcrossDevices across the default device/text-scale matrix

corrections: Only one shared dialog primitive (showAppConfirmDialog) plus synthetic proof-of-concept widgets are currently registered in overflow_guard_test.dart — no individual screen uses the harness yet, so 'the systematic check the rest of the codebase relies on' overstates current adoption. Does not change the core gap or severity.
